habit_scope: Platform stick rafters + ceiling joists on a 1–2 story wood SFR. AF&PA Roof and Ceiling Framing / Figs 56–65. Not roof trusses (m-P09-roof-truss is the ALT). Not timber. Not I-joist rafters. Not SIP. Dry-in / ice is Gap. HUD 8d 6/12 sheathing is folded in — AF&PA silent on roof-panel pennies. ALT to volume truss habit. AF&PA conventional stick. Keep both.
also_known_as: conventional rafter and ceiling joist roof
how_it_is_done: Walls complete and braced. Ceiling joists before rafters on a pitched roof: CMHC — nail ceiling joists after wall framing is complete BUT before rafters, or the rafter thrust pushes the walls out. AF&PA: ceiling joists nailed to exterior plates, to rafter ends, and where they join over interior partitions. Avoid ceiling joists at right angles to rafters (AF&PA Fig 57).

Ridge: AF&PA — 1- or 2-inch thick lumber, 2 inches deeper than the rafters so the plumb cut has full bearing. Rafters opposite each other across the ridge. CMHC: offset at the ridge by not more than their thickness if ceiling joists are lapped at the center wall.
Birdsmouth / notch at the plate (AF&PA Figs 58/62; CMHC). Heel bears over the exterior wall. Toe-nail to the plate or special metal plate fastenings (CLASS, not a brand).

Collar ties DISAGREEMENT — keep both; confirm AHJ. AF&PA: nominal 1x6 or 2x4 in the upper one-third of the attic, every third pair of rafters. FM 5-426: 1x4 / 1x6 / 1x8 / 2x4; 5 ft apart or every third rafter, whichever is less; 4-8d each end of a 1-inch tie; 3-16d each end of a 2-inch tie. Technique not code. CMHC: 2x4 collar ties nailed to each pair on slopes 1:3 or more; ties >8 ft get a 1x4 continuous near center, three 3-in nails each end.

Valley: AF&PA doubled in thickness and 2 inches deeper than adjoining rafters (Fig 60). Hip: single thickness, 2 inches deeper than commons for jack bearing (Fig 61). HUD: in practice hips/valleys one to two sizes larger (e.g. 2x8 or 2x10 hip for 2x6 rafters). CMHC: hip and valley about 50 mm (2 in) deeper. Keep AF&PA doubled-valley vs HUD size-up as both sourced — do not pick a winner.

Cathedral variant (HUD 5.6.2): if ceiling joists or collar ties are eliminated, a structural ridge beam must support the ridge and stop outward thrust. Gable-end studs that do not run to the roof can hinge — not a skip of the ridge beam.
Chimney clearance: AF&PA / CMHC 2 in (50 mm) wood to masonry; CMHC may reduce to 12 mm (1/2 in) for exterior masonry chimneys. Confirm AHJ.

Roof sheathing folded here (AF&PA silent on roof-panel pennies). WSP long dimension perpendicular, continuous ≥2 spans, stamp on the panel (AF&PA). HUD §5.6.4: typically 7/16–5/8 in; nails generally 8d, 6 in o.c. edges and 12 in o.c. intermediate; also 6 in at gable-end framing. High-wind 8d ring-shank 6 in all / 4 in gable is hurricane-prone — not Wasatch/Fontana habit. Dry-in / ice is NOT this Method (gap-P09-ice-underlayment-unsourced). Logan ice barrier is the city sheet. Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack.
trades: framing subcontractors (AF&PA job foreman / inspector — no crew size)
tools_equipment: Named in FM: framing square for rafter layout. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Ceiling joists in (and tied to rafter pairs) before or as rafters go up so walls do not spread (CMHC; AF&PA).
Ridge 2 in deeper than rafters; rafters opposite (AF&PA).
Birdsmouth bearing over the wall (AF&PA; CMHC).
Collar-tie schedule is AF&PA OR FM — keep both; confirm AHJ.
Valley doubled + 2 in deeper (AF&PA); hip 2 in deeper (AF&PA).
Cathedral: structural ridge beam if ties are omitted (HUD).
2 in wood-to-masonry chimney clearance unless AHJ reduces per CMHC exterior-masonry note.
material_classes: collar ties (1x / 2x class — size per AF&PA or FM, not mixed as one schedule)
when_this_beats_habit: This is the AF&PA conventional habit. Use it when the roof is cut up (hips, valleys, dormers) or when the job does not want a truss package. HUD: complex portions of truss roofs often still use rafter techniques. CMHC volume-truss claim is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not a flip of this US conventional habit.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping the ceiling-joist tie (walls spread). Cathedral without a ridge beam. Mixing AF&PA and FM collar schedules on one roof. Treating CMHC Canadian volume as a Fontana/Wasatch habit flip. Walking Utah ice onto Fontana.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They learned it. Volume moved to trusses. What they skip is the joist-to-rafter tie and the 2-in-deeper ridge/hip/valley.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Rafter size/spacing, ridge vs ridge beam, and hip/valley on drawings. Span tables: AF&PA Appendix Item 4; CMHC Tables 29-32 Canadian. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Do not invent IRC R802.
risk_if_swapped_late: Stick vs truss after permit changes interior bearings, hangers, and cut list. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Usual stick roof: ceiling joists tie the walls, rafters sit opposite on a ridge that is 2 inches deeper, birdsmouth on the plate, toenail or a metal plate. Valleys are doubled and 2 inches deeper; hips 2 inches deeper. Sheathing is wood panels the long way across, generally 8d at 6 and 12. Ice felt is not in the assigned US books — Logan’s ice barrier is the city sheet. Do not put a Utah snow pack on a Fontana roof.
spanish_summary: El techo de palo de siempre: viguetas de cielo amarran las paredes, cabios frente a frente en un cumbrera 2 pulgadas más hondo, pata de pájaro en la placa. Los valleys van dobles y 2 pulgadas más hondos; los hips 2 pulgadas más hondos. El forro es panel, generalmente 8d a 6 y 12. El felt de hielo no está en los libros US asignados — en Logan es la hoja de la ciudad. No ponga un paquete de nieve de Utah en un techo de Fontana.

images.caption: AF&PA Fig 56: ceiling joists parallel to rafters, nailed as a structural tie across the building so rafter thrust does not spread the walls. Ridge board; birdsmouth at the plate. Collar beams in the upper attic (text: every third pair, 1x6 or 2x4).
AF&PA Fig 60: valley rafter at two-roof intersection — text: doubled in thickness and two inches deeper than adjoining rafters. Jacks bear on the valley.
AF&PA Fig 61: hip rafter single thickness, two inches deeper than common rafters so jack rafters have full bearing.

Ceiling joists parallel to rafters: joists nail to the double top plate beside each rafter. Collar beams in the upper third, Fig 56 prints 48 in o.c. Layer = joist + rafter both on the plate. AF&PA Fig 56.
Eave: birdsmouth seats the rafter on the double plate; ceiling joist beside the rafter. Heel on the plate, not the toe. AF&PA Fig 62.
Valley rafter: body says doubled AND 2 in deeper than adjoining rafters so jacks get full bearing. AF&PA Fig 60.
Hip rafter: single thickness but 2 in deeper than commons for full jack bearing. AF&PA Fig 61.
Chimney opening: double trimmers and headers. 2 in airspace between chimney and framing. AF&PA Fig 65.
